description: Somos un equipo de estudiantes de Ingeniería en Sistemas y Ciberseguridad, con muchas ganas de aprender y de poner a prueba lo que hemos visto en clase. Para nosotros, el hackathon es una oportunidad de ganar experiencia real, trabajar en equipo bajo presión y aprender de otros participantes y mentores. Estamos muy interesados en trabajar, aplicar todo nuestro esfuerzo y salir con conocimientos que nos ayuden tanto en lo académico como en lo laboral.
summary: Here is the complete translation of your text into professional English, keeping all technical details and links intact: We developed a web-based navigation and safe route planning system for Mars, featuring an exclusive secure login environment with a username and password for astronauts and operators. The platform includes an interactive Martian map that manages 25 different routes for exploration vehicles (rovers). The software evaluates and plots the safest path for the rover based on real Martian terrain data. The algorithm prioritizes the physical integrity of the vehicle, calculating paths that avoid critical hazards such as excessive dust accumulation and large boulders that could damage its components. Before sending crewed missions to Mars, it is essential to use rovers to explore and collect preliminary samples. Protecting this prototype and ensuring it travels along the safest path maximizes its lifespan and the success of space exploration.
details: It is a space routing platform that displays a Martian cartographic map with 25 preconfigured routes. Through a credential-protected control panel, the operator supervises rover movement along paths free of dangerous obstacles. To operate the system, the astronaut or operator logs in with a username and password; subsequently, the system integrates real NASA datasets regarding the Martian surface, and the software evaluates the 25 available routes to determine the option with the lowest physical risk to protect the rover's structure. This prevents mechanical damage from impacts with rocks or getting stuck in dense dust, offers secure centralized control, and facilitates rapid, science-based decision-making. We hope to provide a reliable navigation assistance tool for future Mars missions, ensuring vehicles operate safely while preparing the ground for humanity. The tools, programming languages, and software used include Python, JavaScript, and HTML, working within the Visual Studio Code and Antigravity environment, backed by official NASA data sources such as NASA Open APIs api.nasa.gov, the NASA Open Data Portal (data.nasa.gov), and the Mars autonomous driving AI dataset (ai4mars).
